assignment_criteria.evidence: Production Deliver selects module_deliveries.created_by. CallContract signs the authenticated consumer id. Empty core event/grant provenance and routed system mail use the dedicated core signer. Payload identity never determines sender.

Separate X-Togavsu-Sender-Signature t=,v2= HMAC over v2.<unix>.<sender>.<raw body>; original timestamped v1 header stays unchanged. Both strict sender and legacy verification pass on each actual delivery. Tampering, missing binding, duplicate headers, timestamp mismatch/expiry and empty/wrong keys fail.

VerifyWebhookSender returns authenticated identity. SignWebhookSenderHeaders refuses invalid/reserved module identities; SignCoreWebhookHeaders creates core fixtures. coretest.ReadDelivery and DeliverEvents exercise the production queue and signers.

Two providers linked; Zoom pushes payload claiming Google; duplicate push from Google preserves first pusher. First delivery refused, Zoom unlinked, persisted retry due advanced in test only. Retried sender remains Zoom and body identical. A new push after unlink fails.

MODULE-KIT, module API, API conventions, shared contract docs, generated OpenAPI and CORE-UPDATE-2E describe sender header fields, exact wire framing, compatibility and verification. API contract tests validate required sender headers and unchanged v1 schema.

core is reserved by shared id validation, both manifest readers, local/marketplace installation, both catalog upload forms, and consumer/provider contract links. Module signing refuses core; a queued nonempty created_by=core row is refused by the real pump and remains pending with a reserved-sender error. Core event/grant and system-mail deliveries still verify as core. MODULE-KIT and manifest/catalog docs explain the reservation.
